subject: Security review intake & stakeholder map — next steps and scope clarification
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T09:18:00Z
Subject: Security review intake & stakeholder map — next steps and scope clarification

Thanks for the time on the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps.

High-level summary (from today's discovery):
- Finno is evaluating Redwood for patient-facing summarization and internal search over de-identified transcripts.
- Primary concerns: data residency, audit trail for inference requests, and integration with existing identity/access controls.
- Decision timeline: goal to select vendor by end of May, procurement and legal to engage mid-May.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Penny/Arjun: please share the security questionnaire and the list of people who should be part of the technical security review (IDs: security lead, infra lead, procurement contact).
2) Redwood: we'll produce a focused scope doc that maps which Finno systems would be in scope (API calls, storage, logging) and provide SOC2 artifacts & diagram.
3) Schedule: propose a 60-min security kickoff next week with Finno security + Redwood infra and compliance.

Attached: call-notes + discovery checklist.

Systems I'm planning to include in the scope doc (open to edits):
- API integration: direct HTTPS calls from Finno backend to Redwood hosted inference (customer-managed keys).
- Object storage: temporary S3 for batching (if used) and retention policies.
- Logs & tracing: request IDs, trimmed KV cache traces (no PII), and CloudTrail/Audit log exports.

Decision criteria we've captured: latency SLAs, data isolation & encryption at rest, defined retention & deletion flow, and an SLA-backed incident response.

Please reply with the security contact list and any must-have artifacts (e.g., current SOC2, penetration test report).

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Penny. I've updated the draft scope (see attached call notes) and clarified what's planned for the kickoff. A few clarifications from our side on systems-in-scope so everyone's aligned before Wednesday: 

1) API surface: only server-to-server HTTPS calls from Finno backend -> Redwood hosted inference endpoints; we will not request direct producer access from end-user devices.
2) Storage: temporary S3 staging is in scope for batch ingestion; we recommend a short retention (30 days) by default, configurable by Finno.
3) Telemetry & logs: Redwood stores request metadata (request ID, model variant, token counts, timestamp) for troubleshooting and cost allocation. We disable any long-form content storage by default for healthcare customers unless explicit retention is required.
4) Isolation options: we can offer a dedicated tenant instance (Dedicated) or VPC peering for private deployments if Finno requires that level of isolation — we'll show options and cost delta during the kickoff.

Decision criteria to validate during kickoff: data encryption (in transit & at rest), identity federation options (SAML/SCIM), retention & deletion SLA, and SOC2 + pen-test evidence.

Preliminary pricing signal for procurement: for the usage profile you described (10-50k inference requests/month, mixed batch and interactive) we typically recommend an ARR range of $60k–$180k depending on commit level and whether Dedicated capacity is chosen. This is a placeholder to help Lydia prep — we'll provide a formal quote after the kickoff and scope confirmation.

Looking forward to Wednesday.

Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
